items.title: The RBA has forgotten its job description and must cut rates ASAP
paras: Advertisement Business The economy Inflation Opinion The RBA has forgotten its job description and must cut rates ASAP Ross Garnaut , Peter Dawkins and Jeff Borland November 27, 2026 — 11:45am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Share A A A Monetary policy is not easy. With the imperfect information it has available, the RBA has just one blunt instrument – the cash rate – which has long and variable lags in its uncertain impact. It also has the legal duty to pursue price stability and full employment at the same time.

At its November meeting the board decided, six votes to three, to increase interest rates . The statement expressing the majority view said the labour market remained “a little tight” , without presenting any convincing evidence on this. And subsequent information indicates to the contrary. If the additional information had been available at the time, it would be surprising if the board pulled the lever it has now pulled five times this year.

RBA governor Michele Bullock. Louise Kennerley Just over two weeks later, the October ABS Labour Force Survey showed employment had fallen by 43,500 in the month before that November meeting, and the unemployment rate had increased from 4.7 per cent to 4.9 per cent. The interest rate hikes the RBA had already implemented had taken unemployment from 4.1 per cent to 4.9 per cent — with the earlier rate increases yet to have most of their effects.

At their forthcoming meeting on December 8, in light of this new information, and cognisant of their dual mandate, board members should not be embarrassed to reduce interest rates at least to where they were before the latest hike. The risk of continued large increases in unemployment and reduction in activity greatly exceeds the risk of excess demand triggering acceleration of inflation. It is hard for Australia, with the highest labour force growth in the developed world, to actually have a recession. It would require a huge decline in output per person. But we might get there — with the immense costs that entails.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers is putting together the mid-year economic financial outlook (MYEFO). It is always good to cut any genuinely wasteful or unnecessary public expenditure, but there is no reason to cut the budget to reduce aggregate demand. In particular, there is no evidence of excess demand generating pressures in the labour market for accelerating inflation. We favour moderately tightening fiscal policy and easing monetary policy in current circumstances. That combination yields better outcomes for productivity growth and intergenerational equity.

The RBA, with the rest of us, has been told the MYEFO will be mildly contractionary. That information, with the October labour force survey, make an interest rate cut the logical decision on December 8.

The near-consensus in the financial press is that there is excessive aggregate demand. But if there is excessive demand we would expect it to show up in the labour market. Growth in the Wage Price Index (WPI), the best measure for assessing the impact of wage growth on businesses’ costs, has stayed between 3 and 4 per cent per annum for the past two years. The most recent quarterly WPI numbers suggest much of that growth is coming as catch-up to high price inflation, both current in the case of award wages, and from several years ago for EBAs. So underlying wage inflation attributable to demand conditions is much lower than the headline number.

Careful observation provides no evidence of market wage settlements causing accelerating inflation at any time during the above-target inflation of recent years — even over the extended period when measured unemployment was at or below 4 per cent.

In this context, we question the wisdom of using quarter-by-quarter variations in productivity and therefore unit labour costs as an indicator of labour market pressures for accelerating inflation. Economist Paul Krugman ’s much-quoted dictum that productivity is almost all that matters over the long run has to be read in the whole – and on this matter the long run can be very long.

Underemployment is now much larger relative to employment than it used to be, reducing the NAIRU – the unemployment rate at which inflation accelerates. The NAIRU is properly measured by observation of contemporary labour market dynamics and not by output from macro-econometric models calibrated from historical labour market behaviour. This suggests that unemployment is well above the NAIRU because wage inflation has not been driving up price inflation at unemployment rates significantly below the current level.

Current unemployment of 4.9 per cent, which is expected to rise, is just below the RBA’s model-based estimate of the NAIRU but above some other Australian estimates. It is also above the RBA’s view of the full-employment level of unemployment, which considers a dashboard of labour market indicators.

There may sometimes be a case for interest rates to be raised even if unemployment is at or higher than the NAIRU. It’s pleasing that the RBA recently has given more emphasis to the effects of monetary policy on imported inflation through the exchange rate. And the RBA does have to be concerned about the possibility of entrenched high inflationary expectations leading to prolonged high inflation.

Australia has recently been through three large external price shocks — the COVID disruption of supply chains and the Ukraine and Iran War effects in oil, gas and coal markets. The Iran War shock was still having a large direct effect on prices in the recent CPI data. In extreme conditions, there may be a case for insulating the economy from excessive price shocks of these kinds with pre-emptive tightening of monetary policy to raise the exchange rate — perhaps accompanied by an easing of fiscal policy to maintain full employment. But once the shock has hit the domestic economy, momentum in price increases is only broken quickly by deep recession. Moderate monetary policy accompanied by other measures to reduce inflation will allow gradual reductions of inflation without deep economic downturns.

RBA officers have recently put much more emphasis on inflationary expectations. The transparent statistical measures of inflationary expectations do not support the view that expectations have risen dangerously. The Melbourne Institute surveys cited by the RBA do not point to high inflationary expectations. We have one objective, market-based measure of inflationary expectations: the gap between yields on standard and indexed 10-year bonds. That gap is lower now than six months or a year ago. It has recently suggested average expectations of 2.25 per cent over the next 10 years – below the middle of the target range.

The labour market institutions we have today make any idea of a wage-price spiral far-fetched, as RBA Board member Iain Ross argued convincingly in a recent speech. And the data on wage and price inflation show that prices have put upward pressure on wages and not vice versa.

The law requires the RBA to pursue full employment as well as moderate inflation because it matters. Full employment means a higher standard of living for people who would otherwise not be in work. Those most likely to become unemployed when we depart from the objective include the young, people with a disability and First Nations people. Full employment brings a lower budget deficit, with important implications for intergenerational equity. Full employment favours higher levels of business investment and productivity growth. Confidence in rising employment increases community support for productivity-raising reform – as in the Australian reform eras of the mid- and late twentieth century. In addition, many families are relying on additional hours of work to maintain their living standards and often to meet rising mortgage payments.
When the economy is operating below its potential, everyone pays, through lower earnings growth and less capacity for government to provide services and income support.
Ross Garnaut is the emeritus professor of economics at the University of Melbourne and the Australian National University. He is also a former Australian ambassador to China.
Peter Dawkins is chair of the West of Melbourne Economic Development Alliance and an emeritus professor of economics at Victoria University.
Jeff Borland is Redmond Barry Distinguished Professor of Economics at the University of Melbourne.

items.title: Town with more jobs than people remains excluded from hospitality visa rules
paras: Chiara Bertuccini is a barista at a bakery in Roma, Queensland. ( ABC Southern Qld: Bella Munro )
A tourism body has welcomed changes to working holiday visa rules but says more needs to be done.
The changes require backpackers to do 120 days of regional work instead of the previous 88.
There are concerns staff shortages will continue as hospitality remains excluded in many regional locations.
Chiara Bertuccini serves coffee in Roma, but it is not the town she knew from her childhood.
Born and raised in the small town of Verucchio, about 350 kilometres north-east of Roma in Italy, she now lives and works in a very different Roma.
"I didn't even know there was a place in Australia called Roma," the 32-year-old said.
Chiara Bertuccini says Roma's coffee culture reminds her of home. She loves that people stop to socialise over coffee. ( ABC Southern Qld: Bella Munro )
Ms Bertuccini and her partner Stefano Vignudelli discovered the rural Queensland town on the edge of the outback as backpackers in 2024 and saw a sign in the bakery window looking for staff.
They have worked there ever since, Ms Bertuccini as a barista and Mr Vignudelli in front of house, and have called the town of about 7,000 people home.
While the pair filled the jobs, the worker shortage has persisted in the regional area where positions outnumber people.
Chiara Bertuccini says Roma, Queensland, is a home a long way from home. ( ABC Southern Qld: Bella Munro )
Not-for-profit business advocacy group Roma Commerce and Tourism said the Maranoa region, about 500 kilometres west of Brisbane, had 7,321 jobs but only 6,463 employed residents.
President Peter Stanford said about one-third of the region's hospitality jobs were filled by people born overseas, adding that immigration was vital to keeping small businesses afloat.
"Knowing that we've got more jobs than people available to fill them sort of changes the approach to how businesses can obtain staff and encourage new staff to move to the region," he said.

In an overhaul of the working holiday visa system, the federal government announced in September that a ballot system would reduce second-year visas to 45,000 from 57,000 and third-year visas to 5,000 from 31,000.

After widespread criticism, the government increased third-year visas to 25,000 places and introduced a requirement for backpackers to complete 120 days of regional work instead of the previous 88 days.
Under the new system, which comes into effect in March, hospitality will remain excluded from eligibility for second and third-year visa extensions in many regional locations.
The exceptions are northern Australia, remote and very remote Australia and postcodes 4406, 4416, 4498 and 7215.
While the Queensland postcodes are near the Maranoa, Roma remains classified as outer regional.
Bakery manager Patrick Magee said the working holiday visa uncertainty had added to a longstanding problem for Roma's hospitality industry.
The Roma bakery is struggling with ongoing staff shortages. ( ABC News: Bella Munro )
The bakery, which is the only one in town, has been forced to close its kitchen early each day as it struggles to stay staffed.
Mr Magee moved to Roma from Ireland in 2012, got a job at the bakery and never left, eventually becoming a permanent resident.
Patrick Magee says it has been impossible to keep the business fully staffed since the pandemic. ( ABC Southern Qld: Bella Munro )
Mr Magee said the exclusion of hospitality had a huge impact on the bakery and it had been impossible to keep it fully staffed since the pandemic.
"There just isn't enough Australian-born workers to fill all of the positions that are needed, especially in small towns such as Roma," he said.
Queensland Tourism Industry Council chief executive Natassia Wheeler said while she welcomed the new changes, some gaps remained.
Roma's bakery sits on the corner of the rural town's main street. ( ABC Southern Qld: Bella Munro )
"Some areas across central Queensland have written to us a number of times around the impact that they face not being included from a postcode perspective," she said.
Maranoa MP David Littleproud said there was a reasonable case for towns such as Roma to get an exemption to include hospitality work.
"When you exacerbate it with the fact that you have full employment basically in Roma, that you can't get people to work because they're already working," he said.
"You only have to come and stay here to see, for a night or two, the challenges in the hospitality sector."
Chiara Bertuccini and Stefano Vignudelli worked at the Roma bakery together after they moved to Australia as backpackers. ( ABC Southern Qld: Bella Munro )
Later this month, Ms Bertuccini and Mr Vignudelli are returning to Italy permanently, with a replacement barista already found but no-one to take over the front-of-house role.
Ms Bertuccini said what she loved most about life in Australia was its multiculturalism.
"Australia is made from people that are from outside," Ms Bertuccini said.
"I think it's so important to work in environments that are made from different people, people from different countries."

items.title: Veggie workers allegedly underpaid and illegally hired in Gippsland
paras: The Labour Hire Authority found 20 vegetable farm workers around Bairnsdale were underpaid. ( ABC News: Stephanie Anderson )
Victoria's Labour Hire Authority has discovered the alleged underpayment and illegal employment of 20 workers on vegetable farms around Bairnsdale, Gippsland.
It says workers on three farms were hired through an unlicensed labour provider and underpaid by up to 35 per cent.
Horticulture businesses that hire workers illegally face penalties of up to $660,000.
Three vegetable farms around Bairnsdale in Victoria's east have been caught allegedly underpaying workers and using unlicensed labour hire companies.
Inspectors from the Victorian Labour Hire Authority (LHA) discovered the activity during unannounced visits in the region in recent weeks.
More than 20 workers on three farms were found to be employed through unlicensed labour hire providers.
They were picking and packing vegetables, including broccoli, green beans and lettuce.
During the inspections, LHA officers found records showing the workers were paid up to 35 per cent below the minimum horticulture rate.
Labour Hire Licensing Commissioner Wayne Gatt said it was a "significant concern".
"We know that workers at those locations are most vulnerable to exploitation," he said.
Wayne Gatt says farmers are responsible for checking if labour providers are registered. ( Supplied: Labour Hire Authority )
Mr Gatt said the use of workers hired through unlicensed labour companies was illegal in Victoria.
"People breaking the law face significant penalties in Victoria, up to $660,000 for a corporation.
"If you're an individual that's responsible for a company or responsible for the activity, up to $160,000."
Horticulture is a high-risk industry for worker exploitation due to the seasonal and transitory nature of the work and the high number of migrant workers.
More labour hire inspections are planned for other horticulture regions in Victoria. ( ABC Rural: Warwick Long )
The LHA has stepped up inspections during the busy harvest period, with further visits planned in the Mildura, Yarra Valley and Shepparton areas.
"It's too late when inspectors are at your front gate to check if you're doing the right thing," Mr Gatt said.

At a time when 85 per cent of Australian vegetable growers are considering leaving the industry in the next 12 months because of high costs, according to peak body Aus Veg, Mr Gatt said compliance was even more important.
"If they're competing against people who aren't even paying their workers correct wages, that makes it even harder," he said.
"We know that growers are doing it tough, we know that the margins are tight, but the industry is not supported by people undercutting and acting unlawfully."

items.title: 'Appalling' vandals chainsaw 500yo tree in southern WA
paras: There are deep cut marks on the king jarrah tree, which is about 36 metres high. ( Supplied: DBCA )
Vandals have used a chainsaw to cut part of a 500-year-old king jarrah tree in Western Australia's South West.
Conservationists fear the beloved tree in the Wellington National Park may not survive.
Authorities are waiting on technical advice to see whether the tree can be saved.
Conservationists fear a 500-year-old king jarrah tree in southern Western Australia may not survive after vandals used a chainsaw to cut near its base.
At 36 metres tall, the beloved jarrah is one of the tallest trees at the Wellington National Park, about 193 kilometres south of Perth.
Police are appealing for public assistance as they investigate the incident, which they said occurred sometime between Saturday and Sunday.
Officers said occupants of a silver Jeep, seen in the area in the days following the incident, may be able to assist with inquiries.
The king jarrah tree is thought to be up to 500 years old. ( Supplied: DBCA )
A Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions (DBCA) spokesperson said an arborist had assessed the tree and all options to save it were being considered.
The spokesperson said a chainsaw had been used around the base of the tree, which also has an existing large hollow butt.
"Formal technical advice from the consultant arborist around whether the king jarrah tree can be saved is expected next week," the spokesperson said.
Preston Environment Group convenor Peter Murphy said he was shocked by the incident.
Police are investigating the incident, which they say occurred sometime on the weekend. ( Supplied )
"Looking at the damage on scene photographs … I fear it may have to actually come down," he said.
Vandalism of this kind can attract penalties of up to $10,000 and one year in prison.
Mr Murphy said it was not the first time trees in the Wellington district had been targeted in this fashion.

"It was done by a very experienced tree feller and we can see by the damage that they knew basically how much of the tree to vandalise, knowing quite well that now it constitutes a safety [risk]," he said.
Environmental groups believe vandals targeted the tree to force its removal. ( Supplied )
In 2024, an 800-year-old peppermint tree was mistakenly cut down to a stump by state government contractors.
"The sad part about it is this particular tree was such a huge tourism icon that actually had international significance," he said.
WA Environment Minister Matthew Swinbourn said it was hard to fathom why someone had vandalised the tree.

"In an act that I can only describe as appalling, senseless and heartbreaking, some absolute jerk has seen fit to vandalise the Wellington National Park's iconic king jarrah tree with a chainsaw," he said on social media.
DBCA has closed the site to the public and is urging anyone with information to contact Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or DBCA's Collie or Bunbury offices on 9735 1988 or 9725 4300.

items.title: Data centre proposed for NT station amid water licence dispute
paras: A data centre has been proposed for Singleton Station, a remote cattle station already at the centre of a water licensing controversy. ( ABC Alice Springs: Samantha Jonscher )
An AI company wants to build a hyperscale data centre at Singleton Station, south of Tennant Creek.
The station is already at the centre of a dispute over one of the nation's largest water licences.
The Central Land Council says it will consult with native title holders once it receives a detailed proposal, while environmentalists have vowed to fight the project.

A Central Australian cattle station at the centre of controversy over one of the nation's largest water licences has become the site of the latest proposal to establish a data centre in the Northern Territory.

Environmentalists have labelled the plan for Singleton Station, 130 kilometres south of Tennant Creek, "tone-deaf" and one they will fight "tooth and nail" due to a long-running dispute over a licence granted to owner Fortune Agribusiness to establish a 3,500 hectare irrigated fruit and vegetable farm at the site.

The Northern Territory government granted the company in 2021 the licence to extract 40 billion litres of water annually for 30 years, but native title holders fought the matter all the way to the High Court, which quashed the licence in August.
The decision to grant Singleton Station a water licence to extract 40 billion litres of water annually for 30 years was quashed in the High Court. ( ABC News: Samantha Jonscher )

As the NT government reassesses Fortune Agribusiness's licence to irrigate the Singleton horticulture project, it has been revealed that the company has invested in Central Australia AI (CAAI) and a proposal to establish a hyperscale data centre on the station.

The Victorian-based CAAI did not respond to the ABC's request for an interview, but a LinkedIn post from its chair Russell Board says it is "developing a 1GW+ renewable-led AI and high-performance computing campus".

"The campus will have an integrated power supply comprising 3.3 GWp solar, 10GWh solar storage, 450 MW gas-backed reliability, a private HV grid, water-enabled cooling and strategic fibre in one master-planned platform," the post reads.
CAAI says it is developing a "AI and high-performance computing campus" at Singleton Station. ( ABC Alice Springs: Samantha Jonscher )

An Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) extract shows Fortune Agribusiness holds 25 per cent of CAAI's shares. while a company that shares the same address and a similar name, Fortune AI, owns 37.5 per cent.
One of CAAI's four directors is well-known NT identity Vivian Oldfield, who bought Murranji cattle station, north of Elliott, in September last year.
Murranji Station is the planned home of Project Ares, another hyperscale data centre, which is currently undergoing an NT Environment Protection Authority environmental impact assessment.

In a statement, Fortune Agribusiness said the Singleton proposal was being discussed with the NT government and the Central Land Council (CLC), which represents Indigenous custodians across the Red Centre.
CLC general manager Josie Douglas said the land council was "notified very recently that there was a proposal for a data centre".
Josie Douglas says water use at the proposed data centre will likely be a concern for traditional owners. ( ABC News: Roxanne Fitzgerald )
"It's in the very early stages of development and we expect to receive a full proposal from the company early next year," she said.
She said the CLC's role was "to represent the interests of native title holders and traditional owners, and we will be doing that once we receive a full proposal from the company".

She said she expected water for a data centre would be a concern for those "who have said from the very start water is precious", adding "we need water for the environment and water for country and water for people".

Environmentalists have rejected the data centre plan, with a group of about 30 concerned citizens rallying outside NT Environment Minister Joshua Burgoyne's electorate office in Alice Springs on Thursday morning.
The protesters decorated an office window with droplet-shaped cards featuring messages including "water is life" and "back off NT groundwater".
A group of protesters outside Joshua Burgoyne's office yesterday. ( ABC News: Will Green )
The Arid Lands Environment Centre's Alex Vaughan labelled the data centre proposal as "shocking, outrageous, and tone-deaf".

"Communities across the NT and across this country are resisting AI data centres, but also we want to protect and conserve our groundwater, which is critical to our local economies, environments, cultures and communities," he said.
"It makes one of the largest groundwater grabs in the country even bigger and sees even more free water and more clearing of habitat.
Mr Vaughan was also critical of the NT government's new water laws, which passed parliament on Thursday.
"The Northern Territory already has some of the weakest water laws in the country and these reforms are further gutting the Northern Territory's water laws," he said.
Alex Vaughan says the proposed data centre at Singleton Station is "outrageous". ( ABC Alice Springs: Samantha Jonscher )

Ms Douglas agreed, saying the CLC was concerned that the government was assessing Fortune Agribusiness's water licence after the company had withdrawn its farm proposal from an environmental impact statement (EIS) evaluation.

"In terms of water planning in the NT, it's going backwards, and we have urged Mr Burgoyne not to make a decision on the water licence until he has had full consideration of the environmental impact assessment," she said.
"We would expect he would make a decision based on robust, sound evidence."
Protesters have criticised the CLP government's new water laws, which passed parliament this week. ( ABC News: Will Green )

Fortune Agribusiness said in a statement it had withdrawn because it "considers it appropriate to await the minister's decision before progressing aspects of the EIS that may be affected by that decision".
"Our intention is to ensure the new EIS process can take account of the minister's decision and relevant new and updated scientific information," the statement said.
Mr Burgoyne said the current Fortune Agribusiness water licence under consideration was for the farm, and a data centre project would need separate approval.

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Six people arrested in cross-border drugs smuggling network: ED
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) linked to a cross-border drugs smuggling network . An investigation by the Directorate of Enforcement ( ED ) unearthed a major drug trafficking operation involving the smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India. Lovejit Singh alias Labba , Manjeet Singh alias Manna were arrested on October 11 while Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh and Ramandeep Singh were arrested on October 18 and one Gurpreet Singh was held on October 20, the agency said in a statement. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons ie Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi. They were were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder.

According to the central probe agency the accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs. According to ED , the investigation under PMLA linked to a cross-border drugs smuggling network was initiated based on the seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by DRI and the seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 Kg. of heroin has been seized so far. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where the identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. The accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in the local market. Further, the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles in the second-hand market for trafficking from the storage hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri Madhya Pradesh, and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Previously, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits were attached by the ED . (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: India to grow at 6.8 pc in FY25 and 6.6 pc in FY26: S&P Global Market Intelligence
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): India's growth, although moderating, remains strong with a forecasted average of 6.8 per cent for the fiscal year 2024-25 and 6.6 per cent for 2025-26, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence . Despite a slowdown in economic momentum due to weaker public-sector investment, the outlook for India's economy is buoyed by several positive factors. Easing inflation, favourable monsoon conditions, and increased government social spending are expected to boost household demand. Additionally, healthy corporate balance sheets are playing a vital role in supporting the recovery of private investment. S&P Global Market Intelligence has released its October Global Economic Forecast update, emphasizing a steady global economic expansion supported by policy stimulus, while acknowledging risks from geopolitical factors. The outlook highlights moderating inflation and easing monetary policies as key factors steering the global economy towards a "soft landing."

Ken Wattret, global economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence , remarked, "The global economy is on track for a soft landing, with inflation rates moderating and monetary policy easing becoming more widespread. Still, geopolitical developments have the capacity to dampen or even derail the expansion." Report forecasts an annual real GDP growth rate of 4.3 per cent in 2024 and 4.4 per cent in 2025 for the region excluding China and Japan. Aiding this growth is resilient domestic demand, as regional central banks adopt more accommodative monetary stances. The start of the US Federal Reserve's easing cycle in September is creating more room for interest rate cuts, prompting several central banks, including those in the Philippines, New Zealand, Hong Kong SAR, and Indonesia, to lower rates. S&P Global Market Intelligence underscores that while the global economic outlook remains positive, risks persist. Geopolitical tensions could potentially derail economic progress, especially in regions with heightened uncertainties. Nonetheless, policy measures aimed at stimulating growth, coupled with moderating inflation, are setting the stage for a sustained economic expansion. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: November 27, 2011: The day Roger Federer won a then-record sixth ATP Finals title
paras: Every day, Tennis Majors takes you back to one of the biggest moments in tennis history. On November 27, 2011, Roger Federer and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga clashed for the eighth time in the season

On this day, November 27 in 2011, Roger Federer defeated Jo-Wilfried Tsonga (6-3, 6-7, 6-3) to claim a record sixth crown in the ATP Finals in London. After he finished 1998 as world No 1 in juniors, Federer performed well in his first professional matches: in his five first main tour appearances in 1998-1999, he reached the quarter-finals three times, in Toulouse, Marseille and Rotterdam.

His incredible game amazed the world tennis and soon, he was proclaimed as a likely future world No 1. The Swiss, very emotional during his first years on the tour, eventually mastered his nerves in 2003, when he claimed his first major title at Wimbledon (defeating Mark Philippoussis in the final, 7-6, 6-2, 7-6).
items.impact: A few months later, after triumphing at the Australian Open (defeating Marat Safin in the final, 7-6, 6-4, 6-3), he became world No 1 on February 2, 2004, and he held that spot without a break for 237 weeks.

items.title: He is the only player to beat Jannik Sinner in the Davis Cup but now doesn’t even have a ranking
paras: Jannik Sinner has only ever lost one singles match in his career at the Davis Cup. Sinner, who has just undergone surgery , has been out of action since winning Wimbledon with a knee injury, which forced him to end his season early.

As a result, this has meant that Sinner was unable to represent Italy in the Davis Cup , having chosen not to play in the event last year. The last time Sinner played in the Davis Cup was in 2024, when he helped Italy defend the title after leading his nation to their first title in 47 years.

Sinner has won his last nine consecutive matches in the Davis Cup, across both singles and doubles, with his last defeat coming back in 2023. Which player benefits most from Jannik Sinner missing the 2027 Australian Open?

items.title: What happened the last time Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner did not compete at a Grand Slam event
paras: The Italian superstar suffered a debilitating knee injury in the lead-up to the US Open and has been absent from the Tour ever since.
Sinner underwent knee surgery earlier this week and is now set to spend significantly more time on the sidelines.

“We’ve been in regular touch with Jannik’s team and they’ve confirmed he won’t be joining us for the Australian Open in January following his recent surgery,” Tennis Australia chief Andrew Abdo said in a statement to AFP on Thursday. Tennis fans are now set to witness four consecutive Grand Slam events without the presence of both Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner . You have to go back seven years to locate the last instance in which Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner did not compete in a single major event.

items.title: Andrey Rublev shares his honest opinion about Mirra Andreeva as both a tennis player and person
paras: Andrey Rublev experienced playing alongside Mirra Andreeva at the US Open this year.

Andreeva has won Roland Garros and the WTA Finals this year, in what has been a big breakthrough season for the Russian teenager, who has a big opportunity to become world number one at the start of the 2027 season.

Although they had played an exhibition set together before, the US Open mixed doubles was the first time Andreeva and Rublev had played together in a professional setting. Andreeva and Rublev made it all the way to the semi-finals, beating two-time defending champions Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori en route, before they were beaten by eventual champions Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik . Three months on from playing with Andreeva, Rublev has revealed what he really thinks about his compatriot.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
